doc.title: Hide Tanaka interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 3, 2014

title: Meeting and joining the Junior Mance trio
summary: A Jazz At Noon gig filled in for Mance's bassist; it clicked, and Mance soon hired him as regular bassist after two nights at the Knickerbocker.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: I didn’t realize they had that kind of treatment for tourists. That’s nice. How did you get hooked up with Junior Mance?

I had a gig, Jazz At Noon it’s called. Anyway, they had every Friday at 2 p.m., every Friday they had a guest also. Just famous people. Junior Mance and so many. I think they had Tommy Flanagan, he was one of the guests. And he used to bring his own bass. But at that time the bass player couldn’t make it, so I started to play with him. The first time I played with him it kind of clicked. And already I was living in New York over twenty years. But I never spoke with Junior, and Junior asked me, “how long you have been here?” And I said “over twenty years.” And Junior says “why don’t you call me?” He was joking, you know. Then after that, soon, like two days after, he called me and had a gig at Knickerbocker. That’s when it just happened. And I played Knickerbocker and after we played two days he asked me to be the regular bass player. © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -8-
